missionPremise: The 2026-08-18 operator QA pass filed 21 defects. Traced to source, most of them are one defect: Smart Site has no single subject (the search box, inspect card, compare panel and each export panel held independent parcel targets) and five code paths answer the same parcel questions independently. Sources: _dispatches/2026-08-18_ss-w1_dispatch.md and _catalog/parcel_fact_sheet_contract/CONTRACT_RULES.md, frozen by the planner the same day. AMENDMENT 1 (2026-08-18) then fixed two type defects this lane surfaced (Provenance.atomDids, Setbacks as SetbackAxis) and added UnplaceableParcel/ResolveResult so a parcel that cannot be placed is a designed state rather than a failed Find. AMENDMENT 2 (2026-08-18) then made SetbackAxis.distance nullable and turned atomDids into AtomRef[], closing the two gaps this lane reported after implementing Amendment 1, and established a standing rule: an unrepresentable state gets made representable, never encoded in a sentinel. AMENDMENT 3 then made ParcelGeometry.lotArea nullable and CLOSED the class rather than patching a third instance: every Measurement that can be unavailable is `| null`, and no sentinel ever stands in for absence. AMENDMENT 4 then made FloodZoneShare.areaShare and BuildableEnvelope.derived.areaPctOfLot nullable and re-closed the class by ENUMERATING all twelve numeric fields by hand, after Amendment 3's grep-for-Measurement audit missed the two bare `number` fields that carry the same semantic property. AMENDMENT 4.3 then ruled against this lane's reading of the singleton flood share: a share is 1 ONLY when something measured it as 1, and a set of length one does not imply a share of one.
completionPredicate: packages/parcel-fact-sheet exists carrying the frozen contract verbatim plus real composeVerdict and formatMeasurement with tests; a FactSheetResolver and a SubjectStore exist and every parcel-target consumer reads the store; map centring comes from ParcelGeometry.centroid rather than an address geocode; the four verdict formatters are replaced by one; exports carry a factSheetId and refuse a target that is not the subject; the SearchBar truncation defect is fixed and covered by a test naming 17005 Simsbrook Drive; geocode results are US-filtered server side; the pre-existing suite stays green; a PR is open against main and NOT merged. Under Amendment 1 it additionally requires: the package published under the @empressaio scope; InspectCard reading the sealed sheet instead of running its own two fetches, with the AtomChip popovers and the setback X-ray disclosure both still rendering; and an unplaceable parcel opening its own designed card rather than failing to open. Under Amendment 2 it additionally requires: no sentinel carrier anywhere in the setback path, and a code-section chip keeping its section-number label with no label ever inferred. Under Amendment 3 it additionally requires a single sweep of this lane's modules against the general rule, with anything it catches reported in one pass rather than fixed-and-reported one at a time. Under Amendment 4 it additionally requires the final sweep to be run against that enumeration rather than a grep, with each field read at its construction site.
scopeBasis: Six lanes edit hauska-map in parallel. SS-W1 owns packages/parcel-fact-sheet/**, apps/property-explorer/src/lib/**, src/browse/SearchBar.tsx, src/browse/ExplorerMap.tsx, api/**, and the verdict formatters it deletes. SS-W2 owns InspectCard.tsx, PropertyBriefPanel.tsx, SitePlanExportSection.tsx and TerrainExportSection.tsx RENDERING; P-41 and P-42 own packages/map-renderer/**. Two SS-W2 files were touched, each confined to a data source with no JSX, styling or copy changed, and both are itemised under crossLaneEdits. The InspectCard data-source swap named in the dispatch was NOT performed and the reason is a contract gap, recorded under findings, not a time constraint. SECOND PASS: the planner ruled all five reported items, amended the contract, and directed the InspectCard swap plus a merge with SS-W2's PR #167. SS-W2's branch is merged into this one (one overlapping file, SitePlanExportSection.tsx, auto-merged), so PR #170 now stacks on top of #167 and carries both.

Package renamed to @empressaio/parcel-fact-sheet. @hauska/map-renderer left untouched per the ruling.

amendment2Implemented: A2.1 SetbackAxis.distance nullable - the non-finite carrier is gone from the resolver (setbackAxis now returns null) and from every reader: axisText branches on `distance === null`, the envelope-state projection reads `a?.distance ? ... : null`, and the corner-side comparison uses optional chaining. No sentinel remains in the setback path.

A2.2 atomDids as AtomRef[] - the resolver's atomRefs() helper de-duplicates by did and carries a label: null for a fact's own named atom (a zoning atom is a district lookup, not a code citation) and the served sectionNumber for each code-section atom. The infer-from-the-governing-rule fallback is DELETED; an unlabelled extra ref is dropped rather than dressed up, which mirrors what the shipped chipsForRow can actually draw.

Swept for other sentinels while there and closed one unguarded escape: the envelope summary passed geometry.lotArea.value through verbatim, so a non-finite lot area could propagate into downstream arithmetic. It now follows the old envelope wire's own `?? null` convention.
amendment3Implemented: A3.1 ParcelGeometry.lotArea nullable - the NaN fallthrough is removed at its source in parcel-geometry.ts (buildParcelGeometry now returns null when neither a measured ring nor a CAD acreage exists), and all three arithmetic readers are fixed: the resolver's lotAreaSqFt guard is now a plain `?? null`, the envelope-summary passthrough is a straight optional read, and sheet-to-card-model.ts:187 no longer divides by 43560 unguarded - that one was silently producing a NaN acreage.

A3.2 SWEEP, run once over every module this lane owns rather than instance by instance. Method: grep every Number.NaN, every Measurement construction, and every `?? 0` / `-1` in packages/parcel-fact-sheet/src, apps/property-explorer/src/lib, apps/property-explorer/api and the lane's browse components, then read each hit against the general rule. Loop accumulators were excluded by inspection, not by pattern. It caught two, both bare `number` fields outside the amendment's Measurement audit.

SWEEP CATCH 1, FIXED AT THE CAUSE: BuildableEnvelope.derived.area was being constructed around Number.NaN when the payload served a polygon but no area number and there was no lot area to convert a percentage against. The contract is RIGHT that this measurement stays non-null, so this was a bug in the implementation exactly as the amendment predicted. The polygon IS an area, so it is now measured with the same shoelace-wgs84 method the lot area uses, and only when nothing yields a real number is the envelope honestly `not-derived`.

SWEEP CATCH 2, CONTAINED AND REPORTED: FloodZoneShare.areaShare was writing 0 for an unserved share, which asserts that none of the parcel is in a zone the same record lists. Wire order is now preserved rather than sorted by a fabricated ranking, the upstream's own declared zone stays primaryZone because an unranked list has no largest, and provenance.method distinguishes zone-set-with-shares from zone-set-without-shares so a 0 can never be read as measured.
amendment4Implemented: A4.1 FloodZoneShare.areaShare nullable - an unserved share is null, never 0. The reasoning is carried in a code comment at the construction site because it is the part worth remembering: a fabricated zero is worse than an absence because it is ARITHMETICALLY USABLE - it can be summed, charted or thresholded on, and nothing will look wrong. An absence stops that reader; a fake zero recruits them. The behaviour the amendment makes required is kept: wire order when nothing ranks the zones, the upstream's declared zone as primaryZone, and provenance.method distinguishing zone-set-with-shares from zone-set-without-shares.

A4.2 BuildableEnvelope.derived.areaPctOfLot nullable - removes the LAST Number.NaN in the lane. Readers updated: composeVerdict omits the share from the headline rather than printing one it lacks, and the card projection falls back to showing the AREA, which is the fact that is actually known.

A4.3 - RULED AGAINST this lane's reading, correctly. Both singleton paths (scalar widening and outside-SFHA) now carry areaShare: null. My argument was that shares sum to 1, so a parcel in exactly one zone has all of it in that zone; the arithmetic held and the PREMISE did not. A scalar upstream reports one zone, not that the parcel lies wholly within it, so deriving 1 from set length asserts total containment nobody measured - and destroys exactly the AE-vs-AO information the operator's correction was about. My own Catch 2 argument refuted my other defence: a sibling `method` field does not protect a reader who is reading the number, not its neighbour. A SERVED share of 1 on a real zone set is still 1, because something measured it.

finalEnumeratedSweep.method: Run against Amendment 4's enumeration rather than a grep, which is the point of A4: each of the twelve numeric fields was read AT ITS CONSTRUCTION SITE in this lane's modules, not pattern-matched. Grepping for a type is what missed the two bare `number` fields in the first place.

ParcelGeometry.lotArea - CLEAN. null when neither a measured ring nor a CAD acreage exists (A3.1).

FloodZoneShare.areaShare - CLEAN on every path after A4.3. Set path: null when unserved. Scalar-widening path: null. Outside-SFHA path: null. No share is ever derived from set length. A served share passes through unchanged, including a measured 1. Re-verified by reading all three construction sites, plus a scan for any numeric literal assigned to a contract field across the three modules, which returns only `limit: 1` on the geocode request - a request parameter, not a contract field.

Round 3 (A2): ParcelGeometry.lotArea non-optional, same pattern as A2.1 in a case A2.1 did not name. -> Amendment 3
Round 4 (A3): areaPctOfLot and areaShare are bare numbers carrying the same semantic property, outside a grep-for-Measurement audit. -> Amendment 4

Round 5 (A4): this lane argued a singleton set implies a share of 1. Planner ruled against it - correctly. Not a type defect; an implementer inference that would have fabricated a measurement. -> Amendment 4.3
contractRoundsSummary.note: Every defect surfaced at the point of filling a type from a real payload, never from reading code. The six invariants, which came from observed product defects, never moved across four amendments; only the types moved. The one round that went the other way is worth the same record: the lane inferred a value from set length, and the planner caught it with the lane's own argument about arithmetically usable fabrications.
